line: e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5
teaches: Knowing the right first move is not the same as knowing the line. The tempo losses come two and three moves later, so learn the follow-up or the move you memorised will not help you.
explains: The queen takes back in the centre, one of the two main answers. Most players do find this far, and then run out of preparation — because the point of the position is what happens next. The queen stands on the square White's d-pawn wants, so it will be advanced with gain of time, and the knight coming to c3 will hit the queen again. Two free developing moves for White. That is not a refutation, but it does mean Black has to know exactly where the queen is going before playing it out.
